.45 is a fine round and I'm a fan. 10mm too, but frankly 10mm is a silly choice for a defense weapon for a number of reasons.

9mm is generally recommended for many reasons and if you are getting a first handgun for defense, go 9mm and get some training. Actually, get some training FIRST, then get some more on your gun.

If it's for home defense only, you probably should get a 12ga shotgun. I would actually go with a good quality semi-auto shotgun, because there's less room for user error than with a pump. It's so, so unlikely that a good semi-auto will malfunction once it's broken in and cleaned properly that pump action is not an advantage to someone unfamiliar with shotguns.

In a stressful situation you could fail to fully cycle a pump shotgun if you aren't practiced, or even if you are sometimes. This "short-stroking" is the same reason, by the way, that you shouldn't carry a pistol without a round in the chamber. If you're competent enough to be sure you won't short stroke it, you're competent enough to handle a loaded gun safely.

TLDR: If you want it for home defense, get training, ignore the caliber and fancy-bullet tech-wank that us gun owners are prone to, get a quality firearm in a common caliber, and practice with it. If you enjoy it, then you can start a collection of interesting guns in weird caliber later.
